notes: Exercise library for The Keller Twelve. 72 definitions carried from v1 plus four added for v2 (the wall cable and the step platform). media.still and media.youtubeUrl ship as null on purpose -- Phase 7 fills them. stillSearchTerm is a matching hint for free-exercise-db, NOT a verified slug.

exercises.name: Ab wheel from knees
cues: Roll out only as far as you can keep the lower back flat.
Pull back with the abs, not the arms.
The hardest and best core movement in the room.
commonErrors: Lower back arching at full extension — that's how you hurt it.
Pulling with the shoulders.
exercises.soloSafety: Start with a very short range. If your back arches at all, do planks instead until week 3.

exercises.name: Band face pull
cues: Band around the bar at face height.
Pull towards your forehead with the elbows high and wide, rotating the hands back.
This little movement is the insurance policy on every press you do.
commonErrors: Turning it into a row by dropping the elbows.
Going too heavy and losing the external rotation.
exercises.soloSafety: None. Check the band for nicks and tears — they fail suddenly.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Face_Pull

exercises.progressionNote: Progress by band colour or by stepping further back. Log the band in the set note.

exercises.name: Band lateral raise
cues: Stand on the band, raise to the side with a straight arm.
commonErrors: Shrugging.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Band pull-apart
cues: Arms straight out in front, pull the band apart to the chest, squeeze the shoulder blades.
commonErrors: Bending the elbows.
Shrugging.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Band_Pull_Apart

exercises.name: Barbell back squat
cues: Bar rests on the rear delts, not the neck. Grip it hard and pull it into your back.
Big breath into the belly, brace as if someone is about to punch your stomach, then unrack and take two steps back.
Sit down between the hips. Knees travel forward and out, over the toes.
Drive the whole foot through the floor coming up — don't let the hips shoot up first.
commonErrors: Hips rising before the chest out of the hole — the bar drifts forward and the lower back takes it.
Heels lifting. Usually ankle mobility; widen the stance slightly or elevate the heels.
Knees caving inwards under load. Drop the weight and cue 'knees out' deliberately.
Losing the brace at the bottom. Hold the breath through the whole rep, don't exhale on the way down.
exercises.soloSafety: Set the stand's catch pins just below your bottom position before your first set. If you miss a rep you sit down and the bar lands on the pins. Stay 2 reps short of failure, always, and know how to dump the bar backwards.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Barbell_Squat

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
cues: Feet planted, shoulder blades pinched back and down and held there the whole set.
Small natural arch in the lower back, glutes stay on the bench.
Bar comes down to the lower chest with elbows at 45–60°, not flared to 90°.
Drive up and slightly towards your face, not straight up over the shoulders.
commonErrors: Elbows flared to 90° — the fastest route to shoulder pain in year two.
Losing the shoulder blade position and pressing off a loose, rounded upper back.
Bouncing the bar off the chest.
Hips lifting off the bench to grind a rep out.
exercises.soloSafety: The most dangerous lift in the room for a solo lifter. Set the catch pins at chest height so a failed rep lands on them and not on you. Never take this to failure alone. When in doubt, floor press or use dumbbells — you can always drop those sideways.

exercises.name: Barbell bent-over row
cues: Torso at about 45°, back flat, knees soft.
Pull the bar to your belly button, not your chest.
Control it down. If your torso is rising with every rep, the weight is winning.
commonErrors: Standing up rep by rep until it's a shrug.
Jerking the weight with the lower back.
Rounding the upper back at the bottom of each rep.
exercises.soloSafety: Set it down between sets rather than holding it bent over. Strict beats heavy here for at least six months.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Bent_Over_Barbell_Row

exercises.name: Barbell deadlift
cues: Bar over the middle of the foot, shins almost touching it.
Take the slack out of the bar before you pull — you should hear it click.
Flat back, chest up, then push the floor away rather than yanking the bar up.
Set it down and reset between reps. Every rep starts dead.
commonErrors: Rounding the lower back at the start — usually the bar is too far forward or the hips too low.
Hips shooting up first, turning it into a stiff-leg pull.
Yanking the slack out with a jerk. That's how backs get hurt on light weight.
Hyperextending at the top. Stand up, squeeze the glutes, stop.
exercises.soloSafety: The safest heavy lift to do alone — a missed rep just stays on the floor. Never use a belt to cover up a rounding back, and never do this one for reps to failure.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Barbell_Deadlift

exercises.equipmentNote: Your plates are small-diameter, so a lightly loaded bar starts too low. Stack two 20 kg plates flat and rest each end of the bar on them until the working weight raises it naturally.

exercises.name: Barbell front squat
cues: Bar sits on the front delts, not the hands. Fingers are a shelf, elbows high.
Elbows stay up the whole rep — the moment they drop, the bar rolls forward.
More upright torso than a back squat. Straight down, straight up.
commonErrors: Elbows dropping at the bottom, dumping the bar.
Wrist pain from gripping instead of shelving — use a cross-arm hold if the rack position hurts.
exercises.soloSafety: Easier to bail than a back squat — if you miss, let the bar roll forward off the shoulders and step back. Still set the pins.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Front_Barbell_Squat

exercises.name: Barbell good morning
cues: Bar on the back as for a squat, hinge forward with soft knees, flat back.
Very light loads. This is a hamstring exercise, not a strength lift.
commonErrors: Using squat weight. Start with the empty bar or less.
exercises.soloSafety: Stay very light. A failed good morning has nowhere to go but your spine.

exercises.name: Barbell hip thrust
cues: Shoulder blades on the bench edge, chin tucked, bar across the hips.
Drive through the heels and squeeze the glutes hard at the top for a full second.
Ribs stay down — don't arch the lower back to get higher.
commonErrors: Hyperextending the lower back at the top instead of finishing with the glutes.
Bar digging into the hip bones. Fold the mat over the bar as a pad.
Pushing through the toes rather than the heels.
exercises.soloSafety: Getting under and out from the bar alone is the awkward part. Load it light enough to roll it over your hips and back off unaided.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Barbell_Hip_Thrust

exercises.name: Standing barbell overhead press
cues: Glutes and abs locked so the ribcage doesn't flare.
Head shifts back as the bar passes the face, then pushes through underneath at the top.
Finish with the bar over the middle of your feet, biceps by the ears.
commonErrors: Leaning back to move the weight — that's a standing incline press and it hurts your lower back.
Pressing around the head instead of moving the head out of the way.
Stopping short of a full lockout overhead.
exercises.soloSafety: Check the ceiling and the pipes before your first rep — the basement clearance is not the same everywhere. A failed rep comes down on your head, so stay 2 reps short and lower it to the shoulders under control.
exercises.equipmentNote: This lift progresses in the smallest increments of anything in the programme. A second pair of 1.25 kg plates is the best €10 you'll spend.

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian deadlift
cues: Soft knees, then push the hips backwards like you're closing a car door with them.
Bar stays in contact with the legs the whole way down — if it drifts forward, your lower back takes it.
Stop the moment the hamstrings go tight. That's the bottom, not the floor.
Squeeze the glutes to stand up rather than pulling with the lower back.
commonErrors: Turning it into a squat by bending the knees.
Chasing depth past the hamstring stretch and rounding the back.
Letting the bar swing away from the thighs.
exercises.soloSafety: Start light and stay conservative — this one punishes ego with a tweaked lower back more reliably than anything else in the programme.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Romanian_Deadlift

exercises.name: Bench dip
cues: Hands on the bench edge behind you, feet on the floor. Elbows travel straight back.
Stop at upper-arm-parallel.
commonErrors: Shoulders rolling forward at the bottom.
Going far too deep.
exercises.soloSafety: None, but stop if you feel it in the front of the shoulder joint rather than the triceps.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Bench_Dips

exercises.name: Bodyweight good morning
cues: Hands behind the head, soft knees, hinge to about 45° and back up. Warm-up only.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Bodyweight squat
cues: Full depth, controlled, as a rehearsal of the loaded pattern.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Bodyweight_Squat

exercises.name: Broomstick pass-through
cues: The wooden dowel by the wall, wide grip, over the head and behind. Slow and controlled.
Narrow the grip as the shoulders open up over the weeks.
commonErrors: Grip too narrow too soon, forcing the shoulder.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
cues: Rear foot on the bench, front foot far enough forward that the front knee stays roughly over the ankle.
Drop straight down — the movement is vertical, not a lunge forward.
Torso slightly forward loads the glute; upright loads the quad. Pick one and stay consistent so you can track progress.
commonErrors: Stance too short, which turns it into a knee-crusher.
Pushing off the back foot instead of driving through the front.
Losing balance and rushing the reps. Hold a wall for the first few sessions if needed.
exercises.soloSafety: Dumbbells at the sides only — don't load this on your back while balancing on a bench alone.

exercises.name: Cable face pull
cues: Rope or handle at roughly forehead height.
Pull towards your face with the elbows high and wide.
Rotate the hands back at the end so the knuckles finish pointing behind you.
Light weight, high reps. This is a health movement, not a strength one.
commonErrors: Dropping the elbows, which turns it into a row.
Going heavy and leaning back to move it.
exercises.soloSafety: As safe as it gets. Nothing can fall on you.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Face_Pull

exercises.equipmentNote: Uses the wall-mounted cable. No plate change, which is why it is a superset partner.
exercises.progressionNote: Progress by adding reps, then load. Never sacrifice the elbow position for weight.

exercises.name: Cable triceps pushdown
cues: Elbows pinned to the ribs and they stay there.
Extend fully, squeeze for a beat at the bottom.
Control the way up -- do not let the stack pull your arms back.
commonErrors: Elbows drifting forward, turning it into a press.
Leaning over the handle to use bodyweight.
exercises.soloSafety: Safe. Nothing overhead, nothing to fail under.
exercises.equipmentNote: Uses the wall-mounted cable -- no plate change inside a superset.

exercises.name: Cat-cow
cues: On all fours, alternate arching and rounding the spine slowly, segment by segment.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
cues: Lie face-down on the inclined bench so your lower back does nothing at all.
Pull the elbows back and behind you, pause for a second, lower slowly.
Pure upper-back work — no body English available.
commonErrors: Lifting the chest off the pad to cheat the rep.
exercises.soloSafety: None. The safest rowing variation you own.

exercises.name: Couch stretch
cues: Back knee down, rear foot elevated against the bench or wall. Squeeze the glute of the back leg and stay tall.
45 s per side.
commonErrors: Arching the lower back to get deeper.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Dead bug
cues: Lower back pressed flat into the mat the entire time.
Opposite arm and leg extend slowly; if the back lifts off, shorten the range.
commonErrors: Lower back arching off the mat.
Rushing the reps.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Dead_Bug

exercises.name: Dead hang
cues: Relax into it and let the shoulders stretch. Decompresses everything the squats and rows compressed all week.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Doorway chest stretch
cues: Forearm on the door frame at shoulder height, step through until you feel the chest open. 45 s per side.
commonErrors: Forcing it into the front of the shoulder joint.
exercises.soloSafety: Stop if you feel it in the shoulder joint rather than the chest muscle.

exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
cues: Shoulder blades pinched back into the pad, same as the barbell version.
Lower until you feel a stretch across the chest, press without banging the dumbbells together.
commonErrors: Pressing in an arc that finishes over the face.
Dropping the elbows too low and stressing the shoulder.
exercises.soloSafety: Much safer than the barbell alone — a failed rep gets dropped sideways onto the floor. Check the collars before every set.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Dumbbell_Bench_Press

exercises.name: Dumbbell curl
cues: Elbows at the ribs, supinate as you curl, slow on the way down.
commonErrors: Swinging.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Dumbbell deadlift
cues: Dumbbells outside the feet, hinge down, flat back, drive up through the floor.
commonErrors: Squatting it instead of hinging.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Dumbbell floor press
cues: Lying on the mat, the upper arms stop when the triceps touch the floor.
Elbows at 45°, wrists stacked over the elbows.
Pause briefly on the floor, then press — no bouncing off it.
commonErrors: Slamming the elbows into the floor.
exercises.soloSafety: The safest press you own. There is nowhere for the weight to fall. Use this whenever you're unsure about benching alone.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Dumbbell_Floor_Press

exercises.name: Dumbbell hip thrust
cues: One heavy dumbbell held across the hips. Same pattern as the barbell version.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Standing dumbbell overhead press
cues: Check ceiling clearance first.
Ribs pulled down, glutes squeezed. If you're leaning back to move the weight, it's too heavy.
Press slightly back so the dumbbells finish over your ears.
commonErrors: Lower back arching.
Elbows flaring straight out to the sides at the bottom.
exercises.soloSafety: Safer than the barbell overhead — you can throw the dumbbells forward and away. Still check the ceiling.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Dumbbell_Shoulder_Press

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
cues: Soft knees, push the hips back, dumbbells drag down the front of the thighs.
Stop when the hamstrings scream. Back stays flat throughout.
commonErrors: Dumbbells drifting forward away from the legs.
Rounding at the bottom to reach further.
exercises.soloSafety: None. Set them down if the back position goes.

exercises.name: Dumbbell squat
cues: Dumbbells hang at the sides, or one racked on each shoulder if grip is the limit.
Same squat pattern — hips back and down, knees out.
commonErrors: Grip failing before the legs — that means it's time for a barbell.
exercises.soloSafety: None. Drop them sideways.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Dumbbell_Squat

exercises.name: Easy run
cues: Easy means easy — you should be able to speak a full sentence the whole way.
If you can't breathe through your nose, you're going too fast.
Aasee loop or the Promenade.
commonErrors: Running every run at a moderate-hard pace, which builds nothing and costs recovery.
exercises.soloSafety: None. At your bodyweight, extra cardio is a cost, not a bonus — if a run ever costs you a lifting session, cut the run.

exercises.name: EZ-bar curl
cues: Elbows pinned to the ribs and staying there.
No swinging, no leaning back.
Lower over 3 seconds — the negative is where the arm actually grows.
commonErrors: Swinging the whole torso.
Elbows drifting forward, turning it into a front raise.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Barbell_Curl

exercises.name: EZ-bar skull crusher
cues: Elbows stay pointed at the ceiling and don't drift back.
Lower the bar to just above the forehead or behind it, whichever your elbows prefer.
Extend without locking out hard.
commonErrors: Elbows flaring out wide.
Turning it into a pullover by letting the elbows travel back.
exercises.soloSafety: The bar is over your face. Stay conservative on load, and lower it behind the head rather than dropping it if a rep fails.

exercises.name: Farmer's walk
cues: A dumbbell in each hand, tall posture, brisk walk.
commonErrors: Shrugging.
exercises.soloSafety: Check collars.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Farmers_Walk

exercises.name: 5K time trial
cues: Flat route, measured. Even pacing beats a fast first kilometre.
Target 28–30 min at week 12.
commonErrors: Starting too fast.
exercises.soloSafety: Warm up properly. This is the one hard run in the whole block.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
cues: On the mat, feet flat, drive the hips up and squeeze at the top. Ribs down.
commonErrors: Arching the lower back instead of extending the hips.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
cues: Hold the bell against your sternum, elbows tucked inside the knees.
Heels stay planted, chest tall, sit down between the hips.
Go as deep as you can without the lower back rounding under you — that point is your depth for now.
commonErrors: Letting the bell drift away from the chest, which pulls you forward.
Chasing depth at the cost of a rounded lower back.
exercises.soloSafety: None. If you lose it, push the bell forward and away and step back.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Goblet_Squat

exercises.name: Hammer curl
cues: Neutral grip, thumbs up, the whole set.
Hits the brachialis underneath the biceps, which is what actually pushes the arm wider.
commonErrors: Rotating to a supinated grip mid-rep.
Swinging.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Hanging knee raise
cues: Hang from the pull-up bar, no swinging at all.
Curl the pelvis up towards the ribs rather than just lifting the thighs — that's the difference between hip flexor work and actual abs.
commonErrors: Swinging and using momentum.
Only lifting the knees without any pelvic tilt.
exercises.soloSafety: None. Drop off if the grip goes.

exercises.name: Heavy bag rounds
cues: Wraps or gloves on, always.
Straight punches, move your feet, breathe out on every shot.
Conditioning that doesn't touch your legs before the next squat session.
commonErrors: Punching bare-knuckle. Wrist and knuckle injuries end training blocks.
Standing flat-footed and arm-punching.
Going all-out in round one and dying in round two.
exercises.soloSafety: Check the ceiling mount and chain before each session. Wrap your hands even for light work.

exercises.name: Hollow hold
cues: Lower back pressed into the mat, shoulders and feet lifted, ribs pulled down.
Bend the knees or bring the arms to the sides to make it easier.
commonErrors: Lower back arching — the whole point is that it doesn't.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell press
cues: Set the bench pad to its lower incline notch, roughly 30°.
Lower until you feel a stretch across the upper chest.
Press without banging the dumbbells together at the top.
commonErrors: Setting the incline too steep, turning it into a shoulder press.
Bouncing out of the bottom.
exercises.soloSafety: Getting heavy dumbbells into position on an incline is the awkward part. Kick them up one at a time from the thighs.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Incline_Dumbbell_Press

exercises.name: Incline push-up
cues: Hands on the bench, feet on the floor. The higher the hands, the easier it gets.
commonErrors: Sagging hips.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Incline_Push-Up

exercises.name: Lateral raise
cues: This is where the light purple dumbbells earn their place.
Lead with the elbows, raise to shoulder height, lower slowly over 3 seconds.
If you're swinging, go lighter — there is no such thing as a heavy lateral raise.
commonErrors: Swinging the weight up with the whole body.
Going above shoulder height and shrugging.
Using far too much weight. This is the single most ego-lifted movement in any gym.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Leg swing
cues: Hold a wall, swing one leg front to back, then side to side. Controlled range, not ballistic.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: 90/90 hip switch
cues: Seated, both knees at 90°, rotate from one side to the other under control without using the hands.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Nordic curl negative
cues: Kneel on the mat and anchor your heels under a heavy loaded barbell.
Lower your torso as slowly as you can control, then catch yourself with your hands.
Push back up with the hands and reset. Only the lowering counts.
commonErrors: Bending at the hips instead of staying in one line from knee to shoulder.
Going too fast — the whole exercise is the slow part.
exercises.soloSafety: Expect to fall fast at first; that's normal. Keep your hands ready in front of you and do this on the mat, never on bare concrete.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell row
cues: Knee and same-side hand on the bench, back flat like a tabletop.
Pull the dumbbell to your hip pocket, not your armpit.
Hold for a full second at the top. Your elbow leads, your hand is just a hook.
commonErrors: Rotating the torso to heave the weight up.
Pulling to the armpit, which turns it into a shrug.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id One-Arm_Dumbbell_Row

exercises.name: Overhead dumbbell extension
cues: One dumbbell in both hands overhead, elbows close to the head, lower behind the neck and extend.
commonErrors: Elbows flaring wide.
exercises.soloSafety: Check ceiling clearance. Keep the load modest.

exercises.name: Plank
cues: Squeeze the glutes hard, tuck the ribs down towards the hips.
The second your lower back sags, the set is over — stop and reset rather than holding a bad shape.
commonErrors: Hips sagging.
Holding for time in a broken position.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Plank

exercises.name: Pull-up
cues: Start from a dead hang, shoulders active not slack.
Pull the elbows down into your ribs, chest towards the bar.
Chin clears the bar, then lower all the way down under control.
commonErrors: Kipping and swinging.
Half reps that never reach a dead hang.
Shrugging the shoulders up instead of pulling them down.
exercises.soloSafety: None. Your wall-mounted bar is bolted — check the bolts every few weeks.

exercises.name: Band-assisted pull-up
cues: Loop the band over the bar and put one knee in it.
Always stop one rep before failure.
When you can do 8 assisted, move to a thinner band. When you get one strict rep, you've arrived.
commonErrors: Using a band so thick it does all the work.
Letting the band snap the knee up at the bottom.
exercises.soloSafety: Make sure the band is properly seated over the bar before you load it. A band slipping off mid-rep drops you.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Band_Assisted_Pull-Up

exercises.progressionNote: Load progresses by band thickness, not kilograms. Log the band colour in the set note.

exercises.name: Pull-up negative
cues: Jump or step up to the top position, chin over the bar.
Fight the way down for a full five seconds.
Four of those is a set. This is the single fastest route to your first strict pull-up.
commonErrors: Dropping in two seconds instead of five.
Not starting from a genuine chin-over-bar position.
exercises.soloSafety: None. Don't do these to total exhaustion — a failed negative is a fast drop.
exercises.progressionNote: Progress by adding reps or lengthening the lower to 6–8 s, not by adding weight.

exercises.name: Push-up on handles
cues: The handles let your chest drop below your hands, which is the whole point.
Body in one line from ear to ankle — squeeze the glutes.
Elbows about 45° from the ribs, not flared out wide.
commonErrors: Hips sagging or piking up.
Head dropping forward to fake depth.
Half reps. Chest to handle height or the rep didn't happen.
exercises.soloSafety: None. If 8 reps is impossible, put your hands on the bench and do them at an incline.

exercises.name: Reverse lunge
cues: Step backwards rather than forwards — much kinder on the knees.
Back knee touches lightly, front foot drives you back to standing.
Torso stays tall; don't fold over the front leg.
commonErrors: Stepping too short and putting the knee under load in front of the toes.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Ring dip
cues: Slight forward lean puts it on the chest; upright puts it on the triceps.
Stop when the upper arm reaches parallel — no deeper.
Rings turned out at the top, elbows locked but not hyperextended.
commonErrors: Going too deep and wrecking the front of the shoulder.
Shoulders shrugging up towards the ears — keep them pulled down.
Rings wobbling out of control. Use bench dips until you can hold them still.
exercises.soloSafety: Rings are unstable by design. Set them low enough that your feet can reach the floor if you lose it. Bench dips if you can't control the rings yet.

exercises.name: Ring row
cues: Set the rings low, walk your feet forward and hang underneath.
The more horizontal your body, the harder it gets — that's your difficulty dial.
Pull until the rings touch your chest, shoulder blades pinched together.
commonErrors: Hips sagging so the body isn't a straight line.
Half reps that never reach the chest.
exercises.soloSafety: Check the ring straps and anchor before each session. Feet on the floor means a failed rep just sets you down.

media.stillLicence: Unlicense (public domain) - yuhonas/free-exercise-db, source id Inverted_Row

exercises.progressionNote: Progress by lowering the rings or elevating the feet, not by adding weight. Log the setup in the set note.

exercises.name: Rope skipping
cues: Skip on the interlocking foam mats, never on the bare concrete.
Stay on the balls of the feet with barely-bent knees.
Let the wrists turn the rope, not the arms — big arm circles mean the rope is too long.
commonErrors: Jumping far too high.
Landing flat-footed and heavily.
Going straight into 10 minutes of rope. That's how shin splints start.
exercises.soloSafety: Measure the ceiling before your first session — standing under the rope you want at least 30 cm of clearance above your head, which the basement beams may not give you everywhere.

exercises.name: Run intervals
cues: Hard efforts with genuine easy recovery between, not a moderate slog throughout.
commonErrors: Not recovering enough between efforts, which turns intervals into a tempo run.
exercises.soloSafety: Warm up for at least 5 minutes first.

exercises.name: Seated dumbbell press
cues: Bench upright, back supported. Removes the lower back from the equation entirely.
commonErrors: Letting the head poke forward.
exercises.soloSafety: Lower ceiling clearance needed than standing. Good option if the beams are in the way.

exercises.name: Side plank
cues: Elbow under the shoulder, hips lifted and stacked, body in one line from ear to ankle.
commonErrors: Hips dropping.
Rotating forward.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Single-leg calf raise
cues: One foot on the plate edge, dumbbell in the same-side hand, hold a wall for balance.
commonErrors: Using the wall to push.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
cues: Hinge over one leg, back leg extends behind as a counterweight.
Hips stay square — don't let the back hip open to the ceiling.
commonErrors: Rotating open at the hip.
Going too heavy to balance.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Slider hamstring curl
cues: Lie on your back, heels on a towel or sliders, hips lifted. Slide the feet out and drag them back in with the hamstrings.
commonErrors: Letting the hips drop as the legs extend.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Split squat
cues: Both feet on the floor, one forward one back, and they stay there for the whole set.
Drop the back knee towards the floor without touching it.
commonErrors: Drifting the front foot forward rep by rep.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Standing calf raise
cues: Balls of the feet on the edge of the big tri-grip plate, bar on your back or a dumbbell in one hand.
Full stretch at the bottom, 2-second squeeze at the top.
No bouncing. All that skipping demands calves that can take it.
commonErrors: Bouncing through a tiny range.
Not letting the heel drop below the plate at the bottom.
exercises.soloSafety: Balancing a loaded bar on your back on the edge of a plate is fiddly. Hold a wall, or hold a dumbbell in one hand instead.

exercises.name: Standing hamstring stretch
cues: Heel on a low bench, hinge at the hips with a flat back until you feel the hamstring. 45 s per side.
commonErrors: Rounding the back instead of hinging.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Step-up
cues: Drive through the heel of the top foot.
Do not push off the trailing foot -- that is cheating the rep.
Lower under control; do not drop.
commonErrors: Bouncing off the bottom leg.
A step so high the hip has to hike.
exercises.soloSafety: Check the platform does not slide on the mats before you load it.
exercises.progressionNote: Raise the step before you raise the weight.

exercises.name: Suitcase carry
cues: One heavy dumbbell in one hand, walk the length of the basement without leaning away from it.
Shoulders level, ribs stacked over the hips.
Grip, obliques and posture in one movement — and it makes carrying your shopping home feel like nothing.
commonErrors: Leaning away from the weight.
Hiking the loaded shoulder up.
exercises.soloSafety: Check the collars — this one is all grip, and a plate sliding off mid-walk lands on your foot.

exercises.name: Thoracic rotation
cues: Side-lying or quadruped, rotate the upper back open and follow the hand with the eyes. Hips stay still.
commonErrors: Rotating from the lower back instead of the ribcage.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Walking lunge
cues: Long steps, torso tall, control the descent rather than falling into it.
commonErrors: Needing more floor than the basement has. Reverse lunges if space is tight.
exercises.soloSafety: None.

exercises.name: Wall slide
cues: Back against the wall, forearms flat against it.
Slide the arms up while keeping the forearms and wrists in contact.
Ribs stay down -- do not arch the lower back to get higher.
commonErrors: Arching the lower back off the wall to fake the range.
exercises.soloSafety: A warm-up drill. No risk.
exercises.equipmentNote: A clear stretch of wall. Harder than it looks.
exercises.progressionNote: If the forearms leave the wall, that is your current range. Work there.
